title: The Borrowed Compass
verdict: Iris Ames was responsible for the disappearance of a sealed vial of deep-water sample.
intent: Iris Ames wanted to hide contamination caused by mishandling the sample earlier.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the sample technician logged the final freezer check after everyone returned.
Remove a sealed vial of deep-water sample from its checked location.
Hide the item in a calibration cooler under the salinity bench.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a sealed vial of deep-water sample disappeared from a marine research pier after a water-sampling cruise.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the freezer alarm was silenced for forty seconds.
The physical trace was a trail of cold condensation below the salinity bench.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a pipette case with salt crust near the hinge.
The item could be concealed in a calibration cooler under the salinity bench.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the sample technician knew the cooler had a separate dry compartment.
distractor_cues: a sponsor pressing for early results
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
